sources.entry: Wiki-Go - A modern, feature-rich, databaseless flat-file wiki platform. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-3.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: LeoMoon Wiki-Go is a self-hosted, databaseless flat-file wiki written in Go that stores all content as Markdown files.
summary.what_it_does: Wiki-Go provides a web wiki where documents are plain Markdown files in a directory tree, with no external database required. It supports Markdown editing with emoji shortcodes, Mermaid diagrams, and LaTeX math, plus full-text search with quoted phrases and term inclusion/exclusion. Pages can be organized in nested directories with version history and restore, and file attachments can be uploaded alongside documents. It includes comments with moderation, user roles (admin, editor, viewer), path-based access rules with user groups, and a private wiki mode. Link collections with automatic metadata fetching and interactive Kanban boards inside documents are also described, along with a RESTful API.
use_cases: self-hosted documentation site with access control
how_to_run: git clone <repository> && cd wiki-go && go build -o wiki-go && ./wiki-go
notable: Databaseless: all content, versions, comments and config live as Markdown and YAML files on disk
Interactive Kanban boards created from any document, with drag-and-drop tasks
Path-based access rules with public, private and group-restricted visibility
Document order controlled by numeric slug prefixes such as 1-overview
Built-in native TLS option as well as a reverse-proxy mode
caveats: Non-HTTPS setups need allow_insecure_cookies set to true, which reduces security and is recommended only for trusted networks
Requires Go 1.21 or later to build from source
Demo resets every hour, so it is not a persistent hosted option
